title: Defining Routes and Navigation
description: Create routes, link to them with `<router-link>`, and display views with `<router-view>`.

slides.title: Routes and Views
slides.content:
# Route Configuration

Each route is an object with `path` and `component` (or `components` for named views).

```javascript
const routes = [
  { path: '/', component: Home },
  { path: '/about', component: About },
  { path: '/contact', component: Contact }
]
```

The `path` can contain parameters, wildcards, etc.

slides.title: router-link and router-view
slides.content:
# Navigation

`<router-link>` creates an `<a>` tag that updates the URL without reloading the page. It gets an `active-class` when the route matches.

```html
<router-link to="/">Home</router-link>
<router-link :to="{ name: 'about' }">About</router-link>
```

`<router-view>` is the placeholder where the matched component will be rendered.

```html
<router-view></router-view>
```

slides.title: Example: Simple Navigation
slides.codeSnippet: Home | About | Contact

quizData.question: What is the purpose of `<router-view>` in a Vue Router app?

options.text: To render the matched component for the current route

quizData.explanation: `<router-view>` is the outlet where Vue Router renders the component that matches the current URL.
